headline: Accumulate omitted runs before writing a number
statement: Return every generalized abbreviation of a lowercase word. At each character either keep it or omit it. Replace each maximal consecutive omitted run by its length; adjacent numeric runs must be combined. The unabridged word and the all-omitted count are valid results. Order does not matter.
prerequisites: Basic Python lists, loops, and functions
constraints: The word contains only lowercase English letters.
intuition: Choosing keep or omit creates two branches per character. Delay writing omitted counts until a kept letter breaks the run or the word ends. This pending count prevents invalid adjacent numbers like 11 for two omitted letters.
approach: Track character index i, emitted prefix path, and pending omitted count.
The omit branch increments count without writing characters.
The keep branch flushes count, writes the actual letter, and resets count.
At the end flush any remaining count and save the abbreviation.
correctness: Each binary keep/omit pattern is visited once. Pending counts represent exactly the maximal omitted suffix of the processed prefix. Flushing only at a kept letter or the end creates valid separated numeric runs. Every abbreviation corresponds to one keep/omit pattern, so the result is complete and duplicate-free.
bruteForce: Enumerate 2^n bitmasks and scan each mask to compress omitted runs. This has the same asymptotic output cost but hides the recursive decisions.

complexity.space: O(n^2) auxiliary with copied Python prefixes, excluding output
complexity.explanation: There are 2^n outputs, each of at most n characters. Immutable prefixes along a recursion stack can occupy O(n^2); a mutable token path can reduce auxiliary storage.

pitfalls: Flush a trailing count at the base case.
Do not emit one digit immediately for every omitted letter.
No zero counts should appear in an abbreviation.
